core_obligations: Rewrite the assertion as the statement that the cotangent module of the presentation is the tensor product of the kernel of the presentation with the symmetric algebra (proof lines 2081-2085).
Identify the degree-d part of the kernel with the image of the syzygy module tensored with the symmetric powers of degree d-1, using the cited lemma (proof lines 2085-2092).
Describe the degree-d part of the square of the kernel as the image of the double tensor product of the syzygy module with the smaller symmetric powers (proof lines 2092-2100).

Compute the quotient degree by degree as the cokernel of a map whose target is the syzygy module tensored with the symmetric powers, and identify it with the tensor product with the symmetric algebra of the quotient (proof lines 2100-2108).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the statement about the kernel modulo its square (proof lines 2081-2085).
Compute the graded pieces of the kernel (proof lines 2085-2092).
Compute the graded pieces of the square (proof lines 2092-2100).
Take the quotient degreewise and conclude (proof lines 2100-2109).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the cotangent complex of the symmetric algebra of a module presented as a quotient of a free module, and the proof is a 29-line graded computation. It writes the presentation as a surjection of polynomial rings, identifies the kernel in each degree as the image of the tensor product of the syzygy module with the lower symmetric powers, describes the square of the kernel degreewise, and then computes the quotient degree by degree and recognises the resulting expression as the tensor product of the syzygy module with the symmetric powers of the quotient. The degreewise identification of the kernel and the bookkeeping of the square of the ideal are the substance, and both are displayed.
